Fig. 1. Reasons for attendance at Surveyed Hackathons [1]
3
Practical Application of a Hackathon at the DHBW
Stuttgart
In 2021, the MESH Hackathon was held for the ﬁrst time by the students at the
DHBW Stuttgart. The goal of the student initiative was to bring the individual
locations together annually and to promote networking and exchange. The focus
is on interdisciplinary exchange as well as interdisciplinary solution development
[2]. In 2022, the hackathon was again oﬀered to students of the DHBW Stuttgart.
Due to its proximity to the university, MESH takes an individual approach to
the design of the hackathon. The focus is on solving current problems that can
be traced back to the UN’s 17 SDGs. In addition, the interdisciplinary character
plays a decisive role. Initially, participation is to be made possible for all students
of all disciplines. As already discussed, interdisciplinary collaboration usually
results in better solutions [9]. To ensure that students who are incapable of
coding can also participate in and win a hackathon, two main points must be
taken into account: team formation and the structure of the hackathon.
Care should be taken to ensure a mixed composition of teams. In particular,
this means that the groups are comprised of members that come from diﬀerent
areas of expertise. For example, computer scientists, economists and social sci-
ence students should be present in as many teams as possible. Even if this is not
always possible, due to the number of applications from diﬀerent departments, it
is eminently desirable to ensure comparability. The design of the hackathon can
also help to promote interdisciplinary collaboration [10]. Most hackathons, due
to their history of development, are heavily technically oriented, but this can
be used as a starting point and an evaluation can be made on the basis of dif-
ferentiated characteristics. For the reasons mentioned above, MESH divides the
evaluation form for determining the winners into two parts, ﬁrstly the solution
and secondly the pitch of the solution.

294
D. Beigel et al.
Fig. 2. Evaluation structure of the MESH hackathon [7]
As can be seen in Fig. 2, the best pitch of the team is additionally evaluated,
which is also intended to introduce non-technical students to the hackathon
format. This division makes it possible for all participants to win the hackathon
with their solution. In addition to the beneﬁts for the participating students and
the university through the combination of teaching and practice, the companies
or institutions that provide a challenge for the students also beneﬁt. In order
to support the teams in their development in the best possible way, there were
sessions on current topics and workshops oﬀered. In order to support the teams
in their development in the best possible way, lectures on current topics and
workshops were oﬀered. In addition, mentors were available as support contacts
at all times, either external or provided by the challenge setters, as well as
professors from the university.
4
Practical Outcome
For the MESH hackathon, companies and institutions could submit a problem
they are currently dealing with in their daily business. In order to present a
long-term solution, the corresponding challenges had to be aligned with the
UN’s SDGs. In 2022, almost 200 students, spread out over 4 challenges in the
ﬁelds of mobility, environment, sustainability and health, developed 20 solutions.
As can be seen in Fig. 3, the focus of the participants is on economics and
technology. However, other courses of study apart from computer science were
also represented.
One example that should be highlighted was created in cooperation with a
charity. This organization has long been involved in the integration of refugees
in Germany. The challenge was to oﬀer a range of local activities in which the
refugees could take part together with the locals. In this way, social integration
should be encouraged. However, so far, no possibility for local oﬀers could be
found, so the organization decided to participate in the hackathon with the
question: How can integration oﬀers be designed in rural areas, if the ﬁrst contact
is digital? How can the local or regional connection of young migrants succeed?
After three days of intensive work with a total of six possible digital solu-
tions, one was able to prevail. After the event, committed students joined forces
to further develop the mobile app. In cooperation with the organization, the

How Interdisciplinary Hackathons Foster the Linking of Teaching
295
Fig. 3. Distribution of the study programs of the participants [6]
app is now being developed to the application stage. For this purpose, the orga-
nization provides contacts, monetary means, and the corresponding industry
know-how. The students provide the digital expertise. In the resulting cooper-
ation, a relevant digital solution could be provided through a new approach,
ventured by the charity organization. In this challenge, the mixed team from the
faculties of social work as well as engineering was able to develop a solution that
answered the complex problem by drawing on the theoretical expertise of both
disciplines. Another practical application was demonstrated in cooperation with
a large state bank, which asked the question of what a truly sustainable checking
account could look like. The participants developed various click dummies which
were subsequently discussed in individual meetings with the bank. In this way,
it was possible to show from the perspective of today’s generation how young
people imagine a sustainable green account. Here, too, the ideas for solutions
will be taken up going forward.
In relation to the context of this article, the university’s challenge to stu-
dents can also be mentioned. The challenge posed the following question to the
students: The mobility of the future should be sustainable, social, safe, and con-
nected. How do we succeed in designing this mobility jointly and inclusively, tak-
ing individual needs into account, protecting the environment, and using digital
technologies in a targeted manner? As a result, various digital applications were
developed in addition to intelligent apps for using bicycles on optimal routes.
Here, too, the student teams have the opportunity to develop their ideas further
in cooperation with the university and various accelerators. In summary, many
practical applications have emerged, some of which are being further developed.
It should be noted that due to the positive feedback and the new interdisci-
plinary approach, the course directors are considering integrating the format
into the curriculum as an event. This would give students more time to develop
solutions and ECTS points for successfully completing the hackathon. In addition
to the learning eﬀects, the student teams are oﬀered the opportunity to further
develop their solutions after the actual event. They are then accompanied by
partners from the start-up scene, the challenge setters, and the university, until

they are ready for the market. In cooperation with the university’s Center for
Interdisciplinary Teaching and Research, students of the university are able to
participate in the hackathon as part of a student research project. Companies
or institutions receive valuable new ideas for relevant problems, the cooperat-
ing university has an annual platform for linking theory and practice as well
as for consolidating learning success and transferring theoretical concepts into
practical application. Students beneﬁt from lectures and workshops, knowledge
transfer, and the opportunity to develop the solutions together with companies
and bring them to market [11].
5
Why an Interdisciplinary Hackathon?
By using the format of a hackathon as a teaching-integrated format, various
eﬀects can be achieved. An interdisciplinary hackathon that focuses not on tech-
nical courses but on mixed teams, brings together diﬀerent perspectives. As a
result, comprehensive products are developed as the strengths of all faculties
and ﬁelds of study are put to use. As mentioned earlier, the university itself
poses a challenge as part of the hackathon, based on the curriculum. The inter-
disciplinary, digital hackathon format allows students to apply what they have
learned so far to a practical example. This resembles having your own small busi-
ness, with realistic tasks including business plan development, target audience
deﬁnition, and actual product development and strategic planning. Compared to
other teaching methods, the interdisciplinary hackathon can also promote net-
working, quickly generate new ideas, and allow students to put their skills to use
hands-on.
The disadvantage of the interdisciplinary hackathon from the participants’
point of view is the evaluation. Here, care should be taken to ensure that the
program code is evaluated accordingly. In addition, a period of only a few days
is very short to develop and complete comprehensive solutions. [8] Moreover, the
eﬀort on the part of the organizers is very high, since a number of things must be
taken into account during the organization. However, this is also an advantage,
as the hackathon was organized by students, who were also able to gain practical
experience.
6
Conclusion
Hackathons are also becoming more popular and relevant outside of the actual
invention. Especially in cooperation with universities, companies, and institu-
tions, there is enormous potential in the area of networking, teaching, and prac-
tice, both for students and the universities as an integrated event. Through a
holistic concept and the integration of all faculties and backgrounds, relevant
solutions for current problems emerge that can be implemented. The new app-
roach of interdisciplinary teams, not only consisting of computer scientists, allows
user-relevant solutions to be developed. Also, by linking the sustainability goals,

How Interdisciplinary Hackathons Foster the Linking of Teaching
297
it is ensured that resources ﬂow into the development of truly sustainable solu-
tions and thus a contribution is made to all of us living together. As discussed
earlier, the disadvantages of using the hackathon format are the limited time
available to develop solutions. In addition, the eﬀort required to organize it is
comparatively high. Nevertheless, the possible future integration of the format
into the curriculum shows that it is popular and creates added value for students,
universities, and companies.

Preparation of Students of Engineering
and Pedagogical Specialties for the Development
and Implementation of Interdisciplinary

Abstract. Integration is a modern landmark of humanity in the knowledge and
transformation of the surrounding reality. It is designed, ﬁrstly, to help promote the
world as a whole, and secondly - to provide a deeper and more speciﬁc knowledge
of the laws and characteristics of different structures and systems.
Integration processes take place everywhere - in politics, economics and man-
agement, culture, information and computer technology, manufacturing and agri-
culture, health, education and more. But today, perhaps the greatest interest is
cross-sectoral integration, when the achievements of one industry are actively
used as a means of solving the problems of another.
We see how education integrates not only knowledge of different subjects, but
also different technologies, methods, forms and tools within a single subject or
lesson.
Thus, new knowledge is constantly being formed, which should be taught to
future generations, and this requires constant updating of the content of education.
Integration processes have a special effect on engineering and pedagogical
education, designed to train competent teachers of vocational education, who
must develop and implement interdisciplinary projects to train skilled workers in
changing working conditions.
Hence, the requirements for the professional activity of a skilled worker in the
workplace determine the requirements for his training and, accordingly, the activ-
ities of teachers of vocational education, which, in turn, determines the require-
ments for the training of these teachers. Meeting these requirements is now pos-
sible due to interdisciplinary design involving IT technologies, the use of which
in the process of engineering and pedagogical education and further professional
activities of future engineers-teachers should be synchronized.

Online training · Mixed learning · Hybrid classrooms · Educational tasks

Problem Statement
An integrated result in the educational process can be obtained through interdisciplinar-
ity, which creates the conditions for the implementation of links between different sci-
ences, holistic and integrated application of knowledge and skills in practice, in human
activities and life.
Interdisciplinarity can be traced in the training of future engineers-teachers, namely
the presence in the structure of the educational program of two interrelated areas of
training: pedagogical and technical, and a combination of knowledge of technical and
pedagogical disciplines in performing design tasks.
Modern computer equipment of classrooms in the systems of vocational and higher
engineering and pedagogical education, as well as new opportunities for IT technologies
in education require the improvement of pedagogical technologies. Thus, there is an
urgentneedtodeterminethetypesandmethodsofapplicationofIT-technologiesthatwill
become real, ﬁrstly, the development and implementation of interdisciplinary projects in
engineeringandpedagogicaleducation,andsecondly-trainingfutureengineers-teachers
to develop and implement such projects.
2
Analysis of Recent Research and Publications
Scientiﬁc and practical aspects of the study of interdisciplinary approach in engineer-
ing pedagogy were discussed in detail in a previous publication [3, 4]; the process of
informatization of the educational process in higher education institutions was studied
[1, 6]; psychological and pedagogical foundations of the use of information technology
are reﬂected in the works [2, 4]; the use of information technology in teaching is pre-
sented in [7, 8] The focus is on the possibility of using an interdisciplinary approach
in shaping the content of professional training of future engineers-teachers in higher
education institutions [5].
Summarizing the information on research of scientists on interdisciplinary approach
and foreign experience, we can conclude that: the implementation of interdisciplinary
approach takes place in two formats - at the level of interdisciplinary links (without
violating the independence of the discipline) and the emergence of an integrated product
(integrated); The implementation of the interdisciplinary approach is largely due to tasks,
projects that have interdisciplinary content and are related to the future professional
activity of the specialist.

Mentimeter application
We will consider relevant to the system of engineering and pedagogical education
IT technologies and plan proposals for their selection and application.
Jamboard is a digital board on which participants in the educational process can
write their ideas and store them in the cloud for further access from any device. The use
can mainly be recommended during the CD phase, because this technology provides an
opportunity for a creative approach to the tasks.
Canva, a handy drag-and-drop editor that makes it easy to collaborate while learning
and doing homework. With Canva Learning, educators and teachers can work together
and edit their work in real time: leave comments, add new graphics and edit text. Canva
provides an opportunity to create an original visual support for Ltd., and then can be
used during VD and CD.
The Nearpod platform will be useful for organizing effective online communication
during remote work and in real time. One interesting function of the program will allow
you to turn the usual presentations into gamiﬁed inter-actives and real computer games.
All this can be used both during the OOD stage and during the VD and KD (access
to your materials is provided and it visualizes and gamify content for students). This
technology also makes it possible to use animated tests, PET simulations and analysis
of interesting experiments during VD and KD.
Kahoot! Is a platform that allows you to create evaluation questionnaires. It is a
relatively well-known tool, and many educational centers are already using it to make
learning more interesting and thus enliven the lessons. The educational game rewards
students who answer questionnaires correctly. It is recommended to use this technology
at the stages of VD and KD to test and control the gained knowledge.
Mentimeter. The service can become one of the technological components of
extracurricular activities dedicated to the study of the basics of public speaking. This
resource can be considered from the standpoint of its use in classes of blended learning
format. For example, within the “inverted class” with the help of the service “Mentime-
ter” you can perform input control of knowledge testing and use it to summarize the
lesson. Summing up, we can say that at the stage of OOD, VD and KD can recommend
the use of this technology.
Padlet is a universal online board with an intuitive interface. It can be used for project
work, peer-to-peer interaction, individual tasks or as a tool for gathering information
from all participants in one process in one place. It is used mainly within the stage of
formation of OOD, and under the condition of peer-to-peer training, it can be realized
also during VD and KD.

O. Kovalenko et al.
Consider the algorithms for the use of different IT-technologies at each stage of
educational processes in vocational and engineering-pedagogical education in classroom
learning, online learning and blended learning, including with hybrid audiences.
To use the Jamboard digital board, follow these steps: start a meeting / join a meeting;
click the “Use board” icon; choose the right option; click “Create Board” to add the
Jamboard ﬁle; click “Select from Disk” to open the Jamboard ﬁle from the disk / shared
disk/computer(theJamboardﬁlewillopeninanewtabandthelinkwillbeautomatically
published in the call chat); provide access to the Jamboard ﬁle (if necessary).
We describe the algorithm for using the Canva editor, which is: open Canva and select
the type of design “Presentation”; choose a professional template with slides; upload
your own photos / select images from the service gallery; adjust images, add stylish
ﬁlters and format text; save the presentation.
Work in the Nearpod platform requires pre-registration on the site. After registration,
the user gets to the Nearpod workspace. The following tools can be added to the program:
own content (content), web content (links) and activities (interactive). You can add math
formulas, slides, video and audio ﬁles, a walk in virtual reality and many interactive
activities.
To motivate students in isolation, the speaker recommends visualizing and gamifying
content.
To get started on the Kahoot platform! you must ﬁrst register and create an account.

Business. You need to choose the suitable role.
The algorithm for using the online service Mentimeter is: register or use an account
on social networks. Select the item “New presentation” (New presentation) or another
option - in the “Examples” (Examples) specify a ready-made template and change it.
The service gives each poll an identiﬁcation number, participants can vote in real time.
You can use email or a Google or Microsoft account to sign up for padlet.com.

Veriﬁcation of the effectiveness of the methodology offered to students for the devel-
opment and implementation of a didactic project on the use of IT technologies has been
carried out using empirical methods (surveys, questionnaires).
The results of the survey of future engineers-pedagogues made it possible to deter-
mine in students: stability of motivation, deep understanding of the essence of the content
of tasks (84.62%); relevance of acquired knowledge and skills regarding the development
of didactic projects using IT technologies (80.76%); professional orientation of the pro-
posed tasks (88.46%); the effectiveness of the proposed IT technologies for for solving
speciﬁc tasks (78.85%);creative approach to solving non-standard situations (76.92%);
perseverance and conﬁdence in choosing optimal solutions (73.07%); mobility when
solving speciﬁc tasks (75%), etc.

308
O. Kovalenko et al.
Thus, the method proposed by us for training future engineers-pedagogues is
extremely effective in increasing the level of cognitive interest of students, allows updat-
ing the training material, increases the motivation of students to study; provides profes-
sional orientation and practice-oriented training of students; shows creativity and origi-
nality of ideas in students; provides immediate feedback; increases computer literacy of
students.
Also,accordingtotheresultsofthesurvey,wehavefoundthatfurthermethodological
developments are needed in such aspects as: increasing the number of complex tasks;
increasing the diversity of the student’s psychological portrait and the psychological
characteristics of the study group as a whole (achievement, predominant type of thinking,
predominant type of temperament, attitude to the chosen profession, attitude to the
academic discipline); the use of IT technologies as a means of pedagogical innovation
for frontal, frontal-group, individual and individualized forms of education.
Algorithms developed in the training of engineers and teachers should be imple-
mented for the use of IT technologies. For the development of interdisciplinary projects,
the deﬁnition of the individual phases is necessary for the successful goal. On the one
hand, basic knowledge, the design of integrated content and the development of modern
learning technologies in face-to-face learning, online learning and blended learning must
also be applied using hybrid classrooms. Second, in order to fulﬁll the learning system
aimed at development, the ability of students and skilled workers must be considered in
the development and implementation.
4
Conclusions
Implementing algorithms for the use of IT technologies in the training of engineering
and teaching staff and professionals at every stage will help modernize pedagogical
technologies and their use in classroom, online learning and blended learning, including
hybrid audiences, to expand. To increase the students’ possibilities for individual mastery
of educational materials, to motivate and activate them more to perform the tasks of
professional pedagogical activity.

Didactic Adaptation of Medical Information
for the Formation of Valeological Competence
in Engineering and Pedagogical Training
Denys Kovalenko1
, Alexander Shevchenko1
, Juergen Koeberlein-Kerler2(B)
,
Liudmyla Shtefan1
, and Viktoriia Kovalska1
1 Ukrainian Engineering Pedagogics Academy, Kharkiv, Ukraine
kovalenko_denys@uipa.edu.ua
2 The University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt, Würzburg, Germany
juergen.koeberlein2020@gmail.com
Abstract. The article considers the complex use of methods of aggregation, scal-
ing, balancing and expert assessments as a basis for creating a method of didactic
adaptation of complex medical information as a meaningful basis for the formation
of valeological competence in future teachers of vocational education. Emphasis is
placed on diseases and pathological conditions with controlled and conditionally
controlled risk factors with the highest morbidity and mortality rates in Ukraine
and the world. The analyzed competence includes the basics of a healthy lifestyle,
safebehaviorpatterns,andtheprovisionofemergencycareincriticalsituations.To
implement these basic areas, the discipline “Health Pedagogy” was taken, which is
taught at the Ukrainian Engineering Pedagogics Academy (Kharkiv) for students
of educational levels “Bachelor” and “Master” from Ukraine and Germany. Medi-
cal information is combined here with psychological and pedagogical information
by the method of aggregation. The amount of information is adjusted by scaling
and balancing methods. Feedback on the didactic adaptation of medical informa-
tion was got because of the use of the method of expert assessments and statistical
processing of the results. Based on scaling and balancing methods, simpliﬁcation
of medical terminology and reduction of details of pathogenetic mechanisms of
development of socially signiﬁcant diseases selected for study have been carried
out.
Keywords: Health pedagogy · Engineering and pedagogical education ·
Didactic adaptation method · Aggregation method · Scaling method · Balancing
method · Expert assessments method · Didactics
1
Problem Statement
Modern vocational education, engineering and pedagogical are in a state of active search
for scientiﬁc and practical approaches to creating optimal conditions in the educational
process for the formation of valeological competence in students. It is this competence
that reduces the risk of socially signiﬁcant diseases, becomes one guarantor of the pro-
tection and strengthening of a healthy nation. The formation of valeological competence
© The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2023
M. E. Auer et al. (Eds.): ICL 2022, LNNS 634, pp. 310–318, 2023.
https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-26190-9_32

Didactic Adaptation of Medical Information
311
meets the interests of both the countries of the civilized world and the personal interests
of each person. Health is an indisputable value, and the best approach to maintaining,
restoring or strengthening it is prevention. Primary and secondary disease prevention is
implemented through exposure to controlled and conditionally controlled risk factors,
the content and conditions of negative implementation of which are well known to health
professionals. It is advisable to implement a signiﬁcant part of prevention programs in
the educational space.
The discipline “Health Pedagogy”, taught at the Ukrainian Engineering Pedagogics
Academy since 2019, is based on a group of socially signiﬁcant diseases with the high-
est mortality rates in Ukraine and the world, the study of which distinguishes controlled
and conditionally controlled risk factors. All other valeological disciplines known to
us for non-medical students are based on the principle of emphasizing environmental
issues or physical activity. They also use the traditions of valeology as a separate sci-
ence that developed outside the medical educational environment. Medical science has
accumulated signiﬁcant amounts of information that should be mastered by students of
medical higher education institutions (HEI) and physicians during long life learning.
This information is full of descriptions of complex pathogenetic mechanisms and ter-
minology derived from Latin and Greek. Non-medical students rarely need to master
this amount of medical information. To study the program “Health Pedagogy” it was
necessary to reduce the amount of information, simplify terminology, add didactic issues
(how to teach, what to teach) and psychological and pedagogical information to master
the program of the discipline (motivation to study the discipline and its topics). Thus,
there is a contradiction between the signiﬁcant amount of special medical information
and the insufﬁcient development of scientiﬁc methods for its application in the content
of valeological disciplines.
2
Analysis of Recent Research and Publications
Implementing the state health policy in Ukraine takes place within the framework of
the Concept of Public Health System Development (2016), which provides favorable
conditions for strengthening and maintaining human health as the highest social value. In
December 2022, the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine (Ukrainian Parliament) adopted in ﬁrst
reading Bill No. 4142 “On the Public Health System”, which is a logical continuation of
the development of the national public health system. To carry out public health tasks,
the state monitors diseases in real time; attracts medical workers for preventive work;
develops and implements curricula aimed at acquiring knowledge, skills and abilities
in health care management, taking into account the best European and international
experience; plans and implements information and educational campaigns on disease
prevention, the beneﬁts of a healthy lifestyle, improving medical literacy. Disease’s
prophylaxis is carried out by the joint efforts of specialists and institutions of the health
care system, education, non-government organizations.
The main causes of death of Ukrainians in the previous 2021 were heart attacks
and strokes (over 350 thousand cases), COVID-19 (86 thousand), cancer (74 thousand),
inﬂuenza and pneumonia (over 22 thousand), accidents including about 3.7 thousand
people killed in trafﬁc accidents, alcohol abuse, HIV/AIDS (over 2 thousand), diabetes.

312
D. Kovalenko et al.
The total mortality rate was over 714 thousand (97.5 thousand more than the previous
year), of which about 40% are premature (not related to natural aging) preventable by
preventing the negative realization of risk factors [1, 2]. In 2022, the general trend in all-
cause mortality continues: the highest mortality rates are from diseases of the circulatory
system, neoplasms, COVID-19. In developed countries, the number of prevented deaths
is about a third lower [3].
The leading causes of death from noncommunicable diseases are closely linked. Risk
factors for their development are obviously related to patterns of conscious behavior,
such as overeating, chemical dependence, violation of work and rest, the principles of
nutrition, non-compliance with the rules of hygiene and sanitation, ignoring diseases,
sedentary lifestyle [4]. Conditionally controlled risk factors are considered being the
action of environmental, infectious factors, occupational risks, stress. Because of the
Russian attack on Ukraine, the death rate from external causes (military and civilian
Ukrainians killed by the Russians) has increased, which is also conditionally precau-
tionary because it depends on human actions. Besides military violence, external causes
of death also include criminal violence, accidents and suicides, the level of which can be
reduced through public policy, the quality of medical interventions and the promotion
of safe behaviors [5, 6].
In Ukrainian non-medical HEI, the study of disease prevention principles related to
the causes of death mentioned by us takes place as academic disciplines “Health Ped-
agogy” [7], “Life Safety and Health”, “Fundamentals of Medical Knowledge”. On the
positive side, several curricula in these disciplines include many references to United
Nations and World Health Organization publications, national demographic and medical
statistics, and scientiﬁc and pedagogical work, but lack the structure of medical manuals
and reference books [8]. However, most curricula do not emphasize the principles of
evidence-based medicine, bioethics of experiments with laboratory animals, the obliga-
tion to maintain conﬁdentiality of information received by teachers from students in the
study of valeological disciplines [9].
The medical textbooks we reviewed do not have the accents from the point of view
of modern pedagogy: apart from the list of control questions that allow learning the
material, innovative learning technologies assaults, trainings, etc. The most common
innovative technology in higher medical education are cases [10]. This exacerbates the
problem of didactic adaptation of medical information for non-medical HEI.
3
Statement of Basic Material and the Substantiation
of the Obtained Results
Didactic adaptation of medical information for the discipline of “Health Pedagogy” was
carried out by aggregation, scaling and balancing methods previously used in other ﬁelds
of applied science – mineral chemistry, laboratory medicine, neural network theory,
statistics, information theory and systems analysis, telecommunications, physics and
mathematics.
Thus, the aggregation of information (from the Latin aggregatio) is actually combin-
ing related categories of the general branch of the hierarchy to expand the context. In our

Didactic Adaptation of Medical Information
313
case, medical information is aggregated with psychological and pedagogical informa-
tion. The scaling method, which is traditionally used in the ﬁeld of telecommunications
and software development to change the total bandwidth of information transmission
channels according to their load [11], is used by us in new contexts. For example, at
the beginning of the study of any disease, we used minimal, but the most convincing
information in order to motivate students to study it.
The system analysis method also requires scaling by determining the degree of detail.
Minimal detailing involves setting tasks, research, analysis, preliminary judgment, con-
ﬁrmation, ﬁnal judgment, implementation of the decision. An increase in detail involves
breaking down research stages into sub-stages, increasing feedback elements, and there-
fore increasing the scope. Work with information is characterized by two successive
methods of decomposition and synthesis [12].
The balancing method additionally inﬂuenced the simpliﬁcation of medical infor-
mation because it allowed to optimize it during the control of the success of competence
formation. The criterion for reducing secondary information is its repetition in the course
the minimum number of times.
The expert evaluations method triggers the mechanism of adjusting the content of
the discipline according to the feedback mechanism. Experts in the evaluation of the
materials of the “Health Pedagogy” course were specialists in medical and pedagogical
education and practice.
The purpose of studying the discipline “Health Pedagogy” for students of the engi-
neering and pedagogical proﬁle of the Ukrainian Engineering and Pedagogical Academy
is to form their valeological competence. To achieve this goal, we combined medical and
psychological-pedagogical information, and established connections between informa-
tion and methods of its adaptation. The structural model of didactic adaptation is shown
in Fig. 1.
To realize this goal, we are introducing three blocks: a block of medical information,
a block of methods of its adaptation, and a didactic block. The content of the block
of medical information, which is redundant for students of non-medical educational
institutions, has been simpliﬁed. For this purpose, the information is passed through the
block of methods of its adaptation. At the same time, the scaling of information made
it possible to increase the pedagogical inﬂuence on the level of motivation for health
care by delving into the topics of the discipline that correspond to the personal interests
of students and individual risk factors of their diseases. Aggregation activated students’
cognitive activity due to awareness of their own success in approaching the best models
of safe behavior. Balancing made it possible to evaluate the academic results of training,
and therefore to monitor the success of competence formation. The answer to didactic
questions: “Why and how to teach?”, as well as the use of innovative methods (cases,
trainings, mind maps and mnemonics) allows you to deepen the study of individual
questions of the course.
For the didactic adaptation of medical information by methods of aggregation,
scaling, balancing, system analysis and expert evaluations, the following principles
are applied: 1. expediency; 2. ranking of information; 3. evidence-based medicine;
4. information integrity.

The principle of expediency requires not to abbreviate the information that leads
to the understanding of the negative realization of the risk factors of diseases studied
in the valeological discipline. For example, it is impossible not to discuss the mutual

Didactic Adaptation of Medical Information
315
inﬂuence of such “diseases of civilization” as obesity, coronary disease, hypertension,
atherosclerosis, tendency to thrombosis, diabetes, as well as their risk factors, such as
overeating, abuse of cooking salt, fatty and sweet food, overwork, distress, smoking,
alcohol abuse, sedentary lifestyle, hereditary risks, ignoring symptoms and the need for
medical examination.
The principle of ranking information involves the construction of its hierarchy, the
determination of priority and secondary importance, which affects the decision about
the possibility of reduction. The exclusion of any information should occur without
harming the quality of the formation of valeological competence. Individual details of
the pathogenesis of “diseases of civilization” can be reduced if they are not related to
an understanding of risk factors. There may also be simpliﬁed medical terminology
that has origins in Latin and Greek languages. Information ranking involves the use
of association and dissociation techniques, as well as scaling and balancing methods.
So, for example, when studying the topic of mental health, students are introduced
to the elements of neurolinguistic programming, namely the techniques of association
and dissociation. These techniques are used in “Swish pattern” and “Rapid treatment
of phobias” psychotherapy methods. To perform the techniques, it is ﬁrst necessary
to reduce the image of the problem to the size of a black dot (for dissociation), and
then enlarge the image to the state of a large white canvas (for association). In this
way, sensory self-identiﬁcation is scaled [13, 14]. Similarly, didactic adaptation of large
volumes of information on the topic of mental health is taking place. When looking at
psychiatry in a dissociated, large-scale way, we identiﬁed the topics students need for the
formation of valeological competence: general issues of mental health, accentuation and
psychopathy, endogenous psychoses, conﬂictology, psychological balance, overcoming
stress and phobias. The content of these large chapters has been shortened for teaching in
4 academic hours (3 h). When dealing with the topic of mental health, associate deﬁned
and return excessively abbreviated information, which is a balancing act.
Simpliﬁcation of information must take into account certain limitations, neglecting
whichcandevaluetheadaptedinformation. Thus, it becamemandatoryfor us toadhereto
the principles of evidence-based medicine, which include [15]: randomization of studies,
orientation to the results of studies and experiments with a high level of evidence, namely
statistically reliable randomized double-blind placebo-controlled experiments included
in systematic reviews and the meta-analyses, reproducibility of experiments and others.
Thus, when discussing drug therapy, the teacher should inform students whether they
belong to the group of drugs with proven clinical effectiveness.
The principle of information involves integrity preserving its structure, which is
used to describe nosological forms: description of etiology, pathogenesis, epidemiology,
clinic, diagnosis, prognosis, treatment, prevention of the disease. At the same time, their
following features were taken into account.
The etiology section describes the mechanical, physical, chemical, biological, psy-
chogenic and genetic causes of disease. Infections, mechanical injuries, temperature
factor, radiation, electric current, poisons of plant and animal origin, household and
industrial toxic substances, genetic factors (heredity), distress, violence, working condi-
tions, everyday life and environmental impacts are important for the discipline “Health
Pedagogy”.

316
D. Kovalenko et al.
The pathogenesis section highlights the mechanisms of disease development, the
negative implementation of risk factors, which lays the foundation for further discussion
of prevention options. For medical education, this section includes detailed descriptions
of pathological processes from the molecular level to the level of organs and organ sys-
tems, the mechanisms of the realization of genetic information, stages of infection, life
cycles of parasites, descriptions of the reaction of immune system, other organs and
organ systems to the development of pathology, in response to the pathogen within the
compensatory mechanisms and in the event of compensation failure, stages of patholog-
ical process and their possible duration. The epidemiology section describes the patterns
of occurrence and spread of diseases of various etiologies (infectious, non-infectious,
and trauma) in the population. For infectious diseases, the details of human-to-human
transmission, or animal-to-human transmission (source of infection, contagion, asymp-
tomatic carrier, susceptibility), transmission way (contact, sexual, airborne, fecal-oral,
parenteral) are important. The patterns of disease spread described in this section are
considered for planning their prevention.
The clinic section covers the duration and course of the disease (laboratory param-
eters, symptoms and their incidence of patients of different ages, sex, comorbidities,
heredity) during the incubation, prodromal, manifest and convalescent (recovery) peri-
ods of the disease, its outcome (recovery, death, formation of carriers, disability), com-
plications. The diagnostics section describes laboratory and instrumental methods of
disease diagnosis; data that conﬁrm the diagnosis, help determine the severity and stage
of the disease, monitor the effectiveness of treatment, issues of differential diagnosis.
The treatment section covers approaches to treatment, treatment methods (etiotropic,
pathogenetic, symptomatictherapy, palliativecare) androutines. The prophylaxis section
describes health, pedagogical, socio-economic measures to prevent disease and prevent
the negative implementation of risk factors. Preservation of the traditional structure of
the description of diseases for medical education with the addition of a psychological-
pedagogical block was used by us for the ﬁrst time in the system of valeological education
of Ukraine.
4
Conclusions
All diseases and causes of death have preventable and conditionally preventable causes.
In modern valeological disciplines of engineering and pedagogical education, such risk
factors should be given the greatest attention. Disease prevention is a joint effort of
professionals and the public, but the systematic formation of a healthy lifestyle, safe
behavior and emergency care should be formed in the educational environment. The
instrument of this work is the valeological academic discipline, and the criterion of
success – formation of valeological competence.
The best source of information for the formation of educational valeological pro-
grams is the medical environment (academic and practical). Our method of didactic
adaptation of complex medical information allows to form valeological competence of
future specialists in engineering and pedagogical ﬁeld, to simplify complex medical
information without losing its general structure and details necessary for the formation
of modern ideas about healthy living and prevention of dangerous behavior. The method

Didactic Adaptation of Medical Information
317
is universal, i.e. it can teach the basics of health care for non-medical students of any spe-
cialty. Its use sets a precedent for the widespread dissemination of modern valeological
knowledge in society.
Prospects for further research are to improve methods of didactic adaptation of medi-
cal information for the formation of valeological competence for students of engineering
and pedagogical education.

Video Content Creation Technology to Provide
Web Resources for Distance Learning
and Evaluation, Using Qualimetric Tools
Larysa Bachiieva1
, Juergen Koeberlein-Kerler1,2(B)
, Denys Kovalenko1,2
,
Halyna Yelnykova1,2
, and Larysa Karpova1,2
1 Ukrainian Engineering Pedagogics Academy, Kharkiv, Ukraine
juergen.koeberlein2020@gmail.com, kovalenko_denys@uipa.edu.ua
2 The University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt, Würzburg-Schweinfurt, Germany
Abstract. The article describes the technology for creating video content to pro-
vide web resources for distance learning. The implementation that the authors
describe consists of a sequence of three phases. The ﬁrst is to determine the
ranking of video content, development of the course, education and educational
purpose. The authors also came up to complement the learning phases with reﬂec-
tive activities structured through instructional videos. The second stage is to create
a communicative video content script. In this phase, researchers present a devel-
opment model based on the implementation of the activity approach. The third
stage is choosing a suitable video content creation software. The proposal is a
polyisomorphic model of semantic features to describe educational video content
creation services. Features are deﬁned: instructions for use (purposes); didactic
useful function (characteristics); Ergonomics of the user interface (composition
characters); synchronization of services with other services and (signals of inter-
action with other systems). In addition, a matrix is presented that illustrates the
practical application of the model and reveals the results of the investigation of
identity features. The researchers present a qualimetric-based factor-criteria model
for assessing the effectiveness of instructional video content. The proposed tech-
nology makes it possible to present scientiﬁc approaches to the development and
evaluation of the effectiveness of video content.

of distance learning.
Distance education is a synthetic, integral and humanistic form of education [1].
In which a synthetic environment is a reconstructed multifunctional environment that

2
Analysis of Recent Research and Publications
Historical information on the emergence of educational video ﬁlms and educational
video content is presented in the work of R. Novoselov. It has been noted that the
purpose of creating the ﬁrst educational videos was penetration into hidden phenomena,
slow-motion demonstration of high-speed processes, etc. [4].
A description of the implementation of one of the ﬁrst experimental studies of the
introduction of educational video content into professional training has been given in the
work of T. Noskov et al. The results of the experiment of those times proved that the edu-
cational video allows training students without the involvement of teachers. Key aspects
of its development are the following: deﬁnition of purpose and content; implementation
of ﬁlming; organization of systematic work of students with videos [5].
A new stage in the introduction of educational video content began after 2010, when
the ﬁrst successful projects in the ﬁeld of online education, such as Coursera, Udacity and
Udemy, appeared. Let’s consider the requirements for the purpose, content, methods of
creating and implementing educational video content in the works of modern scientists.
The authors [6] rightly point out that a prerequisite for the use of video content is the
adjustment of each element to support/achieve speciﬁc didactic goals of the academic
discipline. Following them, J. Marinissen and S. Gratama van Andel have noted that
the content of each educational video should be coordinated with the entire educational
context; it is advisable to use various types and actively involve students in work [7].
The classiﬁcation of video types depending on the purpose in the educational process
and eighteen styles of their creation have been given by A. Hansch et al. The authors
present recommendations for the development of educational videos based on the liter-
ature review, a study of the practice of massive open online courses (MOOC) and the
results of semi-structured interviews with practitioners in the ﬁeld of educational video
production [8].

Video Content Creation Technology
321
Modern educational practice allows the teacher to independently develop educational
video content. In their works [9, 10], the authors have noted the main reasons that lead
to complications in the process of their creation. The researchers have pointed out:
teachers’ lack of special communication skills that allow them to “capture” and receive
the attention of listeners; difﬁculties with regulating the emotional state while working
in front of the camera. The authors have emphasized that the issue of measuring the
quality and effectiveness of educational video content needs further development.
Let us give examples of the development and implementation of various types of
educational video content. Thus, the stages of creating video lectures for the course
“Methodology of labor training” on the topic “Methodology of teaching students to
perform technological operations” have been given by [11]. The method of creating
an educational video using the CamStudio program has been presented in [12]. The
work [13] presents the use of screencasting technology in the development of electronic
training aids. In [14], the author has presented the technology of creating short popular
video courses that introduce the essence of a particular science or subject area. The
method of conducting physics classes in the form of a tutorial has been presented in
the work [15]. Thus, the issues of video content development and application in the
educational process are relevant for theory and practice.
Description of educational video content creation services requires scientiﬁc
approaches. In order to formalize any objects or processes, scientists use the modeling
method as the most effective way of learning them.
A model that reﬂects an unambiguous correspondence to a real system functionally
and/or structurallyis calledisomorphic[16]. Thepracticeof developingamodel basedon
isomorphism has been presented by the authors in [17]. The universal polyisomorphic
model has been presented by M. Lazarev for polysystem modeling of the content of
learning technologies [18].
The provisions of the theory of qualimetry and its tools allow assessing individ-
ual aspects of activity. The research of H. Yelnikova presents scientiﬁc approaches to
the implementation of a qualitative toolkit (factor-criterion model) for an objective,
quantitative assessment of any object, subject, phenomenon or process [19].
3
Statement of Basic Material and the Substantiation
of the Obtained Results
In the distance education system, instructional video content should be considered as a
didactic tool that can replace the teacher and ensure the achievement of educational goals.
This requires the application of scientiﬁc approaches to its development and integration
into the didactic structure of the course.
Therefore, in the ﬁrst stage, the engineering teacher should determine the purpose of
creating instructional video content and specify it in the diagnostically formulated edu-
cational goal. Further work should be focused on developing the content of educational
information. To do this, you need to identify the essential elements (concepts, events,
objects, facts, etc.) and make connections between them. The speciﬁcation should take
the form of teaching information and curricula. Implementing the developed content
requires the application of pedagogical theories.

322
L. Bachiieva et al.
One of the concepts that reveals the essence of the learning process is the theory of the
gradual formation of mental actions. It was developed by the teacher and psychologist
P. Halperin in the 1950s. The implementation of theory into practice of the development
of educational video content involves the implementation of components of educational
activities: orientation (OOD), executive (VD), control (CD) and technologies for the
formation of positive motivation for learning. When working with educational video
content, the student needs additional tools to understand the content, process and results
of their activities. Such a powerful tool, in our opinion, is reﬂection (P). Video content
affects the student’s physical senses, so it is a source of external experience. Reﬂection
is a source of inner experience, a way of self-knowledge and a tool of thought. Using
reﬂection requires that the subjects of the educational process determine ways of its
implementation. Through instructional videos, the teacher should encourage students to
understand the purpose of its development. Identifying questions and tasks that represent
the greatest interest or cause the greatest difﬁculty. Analyzing educational outcomes,
formulating suggestions for improvement, and more. The task of the students is to
examine the activities carried out in order to determine their results in order to be able
to increase efﬁciency and performance in the future.
The next stage in implementing video content creation technology is aimed at devel-
oping a communicative scenario that will be presented in an instructional video. The
creation involves the implementation of an engineering teacher of a certain type, as well
as preparatory activities for future changing realities. For this reason, the most produc-
tive approach to studying this process is the activity approach. Its application identiﬁes
and describes the components of the engineering teacher, determines their characteris-
tics, scope and presents the ﬁnal result. Based on the general characteristics of activities
in the structure, of activities to develop a communicative scenario, we have identiﬁed
the following components: formulation of goals; choice of means; Development of a
sequence of phases (process); Product review and correction.
The purpose of developing a communicative scenario should be consistent with and
subordinate to the pedagogical purpose of the lesson topic (topics, etc.). Depending
on the pedagogical task to be solved, we have proposed three types of scenarios. The
pedagogical task involves organizing the educational process in accordance with the
purpose, characteristics of students and the content of educational information. In this
phase, the transformation of pedagogical tasks into communicative ones takes place.
The scenario of the ﬁrst type – information-illustrative – information is reported through
the method of storytelling and explanation. Visual aids are shown (screenshotsof text
documents, natural patterns, additional video fragments, etc.). Through the scenario of
the second type – reproductive – algorithms and technologies for performing the activity
are implemented. The sequence of actions to achieve the planned result. A system of
exercises for the formation of certain skills. The scenario of the third type – part search –
is given a speciﬁc cognitive task. The participation of the students is organized in order
to ﬁnd the right solution when carrying out the individual steps. Motivating elements
(games, competitions, research, interviews, etc.) are used. The means of realizing the
scenario are verbal and non-verbal means of communication. Speciﬁc requirements for
their use in educational video content are presented in the study [3].

Video Content Creation Technology
323
The sequence of script development includes the following phases: writing a logline
(states the main idea of the script in a concise form of up to 25 words); Preparation of
a synopsis (summary of the content of the screenplay); Development of the treatment
(presentation of the content by the author with a description of the details, the most
effective and interesting moments); Screenwriting (includes a detailed episode descrip-
tion, text, etc.). Further work of the engineering teacher is to check the implementation
of the script, i.e. rehearsals and rehearsals. If necessary, a correction is made. The next
stage is the implementation of the designed scenario and implementing video recording
of instructional video content. At this stage, the engineer-pedagogue must decide on the
service to be used, choosing from a large number of those offered by the developers.
Based on the results of modeling as a scientiﬁc method of cognition, adaptation of
examples of the development of a polyisomorphic model of semantic features [17, 18] to
the conditions of our research, we have developed a polyisomorphic model of semantic
features for the description of services for creating educational video content (1):
Tv. = {Uv., Fv, Ev, Cv},

The factors and criteria are determined by experts in their importance. We note that
the factors, criteria and their importance are determined by experts. To determine the
signiﬁcance, the members of the expert group assign a point ranking to each factor
(criterion), the result is the ratio of the sum of point rankings by factor (criterion) to
the total sum of point rankings. The model is created in the Excel spreadsheet editor.
Coefﬁcient of conformity of the standard (Xn) it is based on the analysis of instructional
video content, study of instructional materials, questionnaires or surveys of students.
Subsequent calculations allow us to determine the overall rating of video.
4
Conclusions
The technology for creating video content and delivering web resources for distance
learning was developed and implemented at the Ukrainian Academy of Engineering and
Pedagogy. Based on scientiﬁc approaches and practical developments, the authors have
developed the following: implementation stages of video content creation technology;
the model for developing a communicative scenario; a polyisomorphic model presenting
the results of your research with semantic features in a map-matrix; the factor-criterion
model for evaluating the effectiveness of video content. The results of the conﬁrmatory
and formative experimental research conﬁrming the positive impact of the technology
on the quality and effectiveness of educational video content will be presented in the
next publications.

Preparing Engineering Teacher Students
for the Challenges of Vocational Training
Ildikó Holik(B)
Óbuda University, Budapest, Hungary
holik.ildiko@tmpk.uni-obuda.hu
Abstract. Today’s technological, economic and labour market changes also have
an impact on Hungarian vocational training. The Vocational Training 4.0 strategy
determines the system-wide renewal and further development of vocational train-
ing and adult education. At the same time, innovation poses a huge challenge for
teachers in vocational training. Vocational teacher education, including engineer-
ing teacher education, also faces these challenges, as it is this area that prepares
trainee teachers for working in vocational training. The paper presents the impact
of Industry 4.0 on vocational training in Hungary and addresses the question of
how vocational teachers can prepare for the changes in this ﬁeld. Based on the
results of a questionnaire survey conducted among engineering teacher students,
it draws attention to the need for methodological renewal. It presents the possibili-
ties of content and methodological development of engineering teacher education
through examples.
Keywords: Vocational training · Engineering teacher education · Changes
1
Introduction
As a result of technological innovations and the accelerating pace of change in the econ-
omy and the labour market, there is an increasing need for a vocational training system
that can adapt quickly to the needs of the labour market. In Hungary, Industry 4.0 [1], that
is, the fourth industrial revolution has led to the development of the Vocational Train-
ing 4.0 strategy [2], which deﬁnes the system-wide renewal and further development of
vocational training and adult education.
The new strategy rests on three pillars:
1. Career opportunities (a simple, transparent, continuous system; attractive, 5-year
secondary modern school; a system of grants),
2. Attractive environment (infrastructure; high quality workshops with modern equip-
ment; ensuring the conditions for dual training; digital content; modern teaching
technologies),
3. Up-to-date teachers’ knowledge (accredited teacher education programmes in com-
pany venues; more ﬂexible trainings for engineering and vocational teachers; devel-
oping the methodology for small-group remedial teaching; preparation for mentor-
ing tasks; a new qualiﬁcation system based on the speciﬁcs of vocational training;
development of a career model; adjustment to market wages; digital assistants) [2].

Preparing Engineering Teacher Students for the Challenges
329
The innovations pose a huge challenge to the teachers working in vocational training.
Vocational teacher education, including engineering teacher education, also faces these
challenges, as its task is to prepare students in the areas of pedagogy, psychology and
subject-speciﬁc methodology for their work in vocational training.
2
Changes in Vocational Training and in Vocational Teacher
Education
Vocational training in Hungary grapples with numerous problems, which has led to the
structural and content renewal of its system.
In Hungary, fewer students participate in vocational training than the European
average. However, the dropout rate is high (12%).
A lot of students opt out from vocational training after the matriculation examina-
tion, without one or two additional years leading to a technician qualiﬁcation (46%). A
signiﬁcant number of students wish to work in a trade different from what they learnt in
vocational training.
An ever-growing number of students (almost 30%) arrive from primary education
with a lack of competencies so serious that it makes then unable to acquire competitive
knowledge. There is also a signiﬁcant difference in students’ performance depending on
their family backgrounds [2].
The structural and content transformation of vocational training was ﬁrst introduced
in September 2020 and follows a gradual introduction schedule. The aim of the new
vocational training structure is to provide ﬂexible learning pathways and continuity for
everyone. Those who start their studies at a grammar school, technical school or voca-
tional school can equally enter higher education or the labour market with a competitive
vocational diploma built upon their primary or secondary school qualiﬁcations.
However, the process of renewal and transformation poses a number of challenges to
teachers working in vocational training. With the introduction of the List of Professions,
new professions have emerged and the content of the Training and Output Requirements
and the Curricula have been renewed, but the preparation of teachers for these rapid
changes is lagging behind.
The two school types of the new, school-based vocational training system are the
5-year vocational school, which provides a high school diploma as well as a techni-
cal qualiﬁcation, and the 3-year vocational training school, which provides vocational
training. Dual training is key to both school types. However, the personal and material
conditions of secondary vocational education vary greatly from one vocational training
institution to another. Raising the standard of vocational training is still a key issue.
In addition to structural changes, online teaching, introduced during the pandemic,
[3]hasalsobeenamajorchallengeforteachers.Theimplementationofeffectiveteaching
required openness, ﬂexibility and the development of ICT skills on their part [4].
The high average age and the shortage of teachers, especially new graduates, are also
problems in vocational training. The average age of teachers has increased signiﬁcantly
recently. “A very strong wave of retirement is to be expected over the next three years
among teachers, who are aging at the same rate as the general population. As a result,
the replacement of teachers of theoretical and practical professional subjects will be a

330
I. Holik
problem even in the short term. Those who graduate from full-time vocational teacher
education cannot replace this number…” reads a statement made by the Ministry of
Innovation and Technology (ITM) in 2019, entitled “Medium-term professional strategy
for the renewal of vocational training and adult education” [2].
Therefore, one of the goals of the development of vocational training is to ensure
an adequate number of teachers teaching theoretical and practical professional subjects,
and to improve the retention capacity of the teaching profession.
Many factors reduce the attractiveness of vocational training, so the enrolment of
teachers is not smooth. Of the full-time BSc engineering graduates who continue their
studies in one of the MA programmes at our university, only a few choose engineering
teacher education.
The following conditions would need to be ensured for young people to choose a
career as a vocational teacher and for teachers of vocational subjects to remain in the
profession [2]:
• Competitive salary and the acknowledgement and remuneration of individual achieve-
ments,
• Predictability, vision, career opportunities,
• Inspiring work atmosphere,
• Availability of quality educational equipment,
• Supporting and facilitating additional and administrative tasks,
• Providing opportunities for in-service training and professional development,
• Social esteem.
3
Challenges in Engineering Teacher Education
Our university offers MA-level engineering teacher education with six specializations
(mechanics and mechatronics; civil and security protection; electro-technics and elec-
tronics; informatics; technical-economics; light and printing industry). The duration of
the training for students possessing a BSc (college level) degree in their ﬁeld of spe-
cialisation is four terms, and following a college level teaching qualiﬁcation is two
terms.
Most of the students take part in correspondence courses and several of them have
several years of teaching experience, primarily in vocational training. However, another
part of the students do not yet have any teaching experience, so they are considered new
to the teaching profession, even though they have signiﬁcant work experience in other
ﬁelds. This is a student population that is already a challenge for educators in terms of
shaping their attitudes.
The elements of teacher qualiﬁcation in teacher education in Hungary are the fol-
lowing: a) specialist knowledge of one’s subject, b) theoretical and practical knowledge
of pedagogy and psychology; subject-speciﬁc methodology, along with the required
skills and attitudes, and c) as part of the pedagogical, psychological and teaching prac-
tice acquired in parallel with the training, career knowledge and career socialization
practices, teaching practices and a contiguous individual school practice completed in a
public education or vocational training institution.

Preparing Engineering Teacher Students for the Challenges
331
Teacher education must prepare prospective engineering teachers for the challenges
of vocational training and the changing pedagogical environment. Firstly, it requires
content renewal. In engineering teacher education, the knowledge of the ﬁeld includes
the state-of-the-art technical, technological and information systems applicable in the
ﬁeld of engineering, changes in the macro- and micro-environment of technical and
engineering activities, as well as domestic and international trends of the above. One
of the new elements in teacher education is the practice related to collaboration space,
educational technology innovation and artiﬁcial intelligence, which deals with the appli-
cation of modern technological knowledge in education. Secondly, there is also a need for
methodological renewal –not onlyinterms of theacquisitionof digital teachingmethods,
but also in collaborative learning [5], cooperative education [6], problem-based learning,
research-based learning, project teaching and developmental assessment [7]. One of the
keys to teacher work and student success is the selection and adequate application of the
most appropriate pedagogical method(s) from the rich methodological repertoire.
Industry 4.0 has also changed competency requirements. According to the Future
of Jobs Report (by the Word Economic Forum), the key competencies for 2020 are: 1.
Complex problem solving, 2. Critical thinking, 3. Creativity, 4. Managing people, 5.
Teamwork, 6. Emotional intelligence, 7. Judgment and decision making, 8. Service and
orientation, 9. Negotiation, 10. Cognitive ﬂexibility [8]. These expectations also appear
in teacher education. Graduating vocational teachers can effectively develop the above
competencies of secondary school students by using participatory and collaborative
methods that activate learners.
During the pandemic, when educational institutions switched to on-line teaching,
the questions that became apparent at the national level were how teachers could cope
with the situation, how they could plan on-line teaching and how they could develop
and apply digital curricula. Our teacher education programme also prepares students
for these current challenges: the creation of digital tasks, the development of digital
curricula, also taking the opportunities for gamiﬁcation [9, 10].
In addition to the above, in engineering teacher education, we must pay particular
attention to the areas of special needs education, the possibilities of educating under-
motivated students, the risk of dropping out of school and the need for prevention. All
these problems are current in Hungarian vocational training today.
4
The Necessity for Methodological Renewal
The need for methodological renewal was highlighted by our questionnaire survey con-
ducted among 77 students in engineering teacher education. The aim of the research
was to map the methodological culture of vocational teachers. The research questions
were the following: To what extent do the traditions, routines and the expectations of
their environment inﬂuence respondents’ choices of teaching methods? What methods
do they prefer? How open are they to innovation?
Characteristics of the participants of the survey: their average age is 39.96 years.
65.4% of them work as teachers and 47% teach in vocational training. 28.6% of respon-
dents have less than one year of teaching experience and 37.7% have only been teaching
for a maximum of 5 years.

332
I. Holik

the traditional, frontal teaching methods that they had seen and learned from their own
former teachers (Table 1). Although they have learnt and are familiar with new, atypical
methods, few use them in practice (Table 2).
It is worth noting to what a great extent the example of one’s own teachers is dominant
over didactic, methodological and practical training and in-service training.

Three methods were highlighted by respondents which they used in every lesson:
explanation (61.4% of respondents), discussion (46.5%) and lecture (42.5%).
Of the methods based on student activity, even though rarely used by respondents,
the cooperative methods are the most popular (average score: 3.01). However, simulation
(2.57), presentation (2.54), the project method (2.49), games (2.37) and role-play (1.87)
are hardly ever present in students’ methodological repertoire.
The traditional methods based on frontal work are mainly used by novice teachers,
while the so-called atypical methods, based on the activity of students, are used by more
experienced teachers.

cooperative and collaborative teaching methods, research and problem-based learning,

In engineering teacher education, we can support the methodological renewal by
